_comment: GENERATED from the private leak corpus by claude-bpx bridge/scripts/cpa-corpus-subset.js. Do not hand-edit: the cases are verbatim copies and cases_sha256 is checked by leak_corpus_test.go.

cases.incident: FALLBACK SHAPE SURVIVES BYTE-FOR-BYTE (t_e121b418 root cause; CPA side Kyzcreig/CLIProxyAPI#18, t_d27c2365; card t_4c8005fc). The CLI 2.1.283 retry after a refusal carries a top-level opaque `fallback_credit_token` (server-minted, expires in ~5 min) and, on the opt-in request, a `fallbacks` body key. Upstream rejects ANY edit: the CPA#18 replay table shows 400 'fallback_credit_token: output_config.effort must be omitted', then 400 'has expired' once the value changed. apx cch normalization (src/cch.js CCH_EXCLUDED_KEYS) already treats both keys as outside the signed body. MEASURED 2026-10-02 on claude-apx master: processBody('hermes' profile) rewrote the brand-like substring INSIDE the token value. The probe token deliberately carries a brand-like substring so any content scrubber that walks top-level values goes red; the message content carries the same word so the case also proves the scrubber was live on that body. This case pins: the token key and its opaque value reach the wire byte-identical (a scrubber or aliaser that touches the value fails here).

excluded.bpx: bpx never holds the upstream request body: it hands text to the genuine CLI, which mints fallbacks/fallback_credit_token itself. The body-rewriting hop on that path is DPX (CLIProxyAPI contentalias.Prepare), covered by external_consumers cpa.
excluded.pool: the relay forwards body bytes untouched and runs no content scrubber; its one body edit (capacity_rung) rewrites only `model` via a json round-trip, which preserves string values.
